descriptors.definition: The standard prescribes accounting treatment for inventories, specifically addressing cost determination, expense recognition, and write-downs to net realizable value. It provides guidance on measurement techniques and cost formulas.
inclusion: guidance for determining inventory cost
guidance for subsequent recognition as an expense
measurement techniques like standard cost and retail method
exclusion: biological assets related to agricultural activity
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general inventory accounting and specialized financial instrument or biological asset frameworks.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies to all inventories except financial instruments, biological assets at the point of harvest, and certain producer or broker-trader inventories measured at fair value. It outlines the boundaries of applicability for different asset classes.
inclusion: all general inventories
harvested agricultural produce after initial fair value recognition
exclusion: financial instruments under Ind AS 32 and Ind AS 109
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates between standard inventories and scoped-out items such as financial instruments and biological assets.

descriptors.definition: Inventories comprise assets held for sale in the ordinary course of business, in the process of production for such sale, or as materials to be consumed in production or service rendering. Net realisable value represents estimated selling price less estimated costs of completion and disposal.
inclusion: goods held for resale
finished goods and work in progress
materials and supplies awaiting production use
exclusion: costs to fulfill a contract accounted under Ind AS 115 that do not form inventories
secondary packing materials and publicity materials
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between primary packing material included in inventory and secondary packing or publicity costs excluded from inventory.

descriptors.definition: Inventories must be measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Total cost comprises purchase costs, conversion costs, and other expenses incurred in bringing the items to their present location and condition.
terminology: lower of cost and net realisable value
inclusion: purchase price and import duties
transport and handling charges
direct and systematic allocation of production overheads
exclusion: trade discounts and rebates deducted from purchase price
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes purchase price components from subsequent handling and conversion expenditures.

descriptors.definition: Inventory carrying amounts are recognized as an expense in the period when the related revenue is recognized or when write-downs and losses occur. Reversals of previous write-downs reduce the expense amount in the period they occur.
inclusion: carrying amount of sold inventory recognized as expense
losses and write-downs to net realisable value
allocations to other asset accounts like property, plant and equipment
exclusion: immediate direct expensing when allocated to self-constructed assets before depreciation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes immediate expense recognition from capitalization into other asset accounts such as property, plant and equipment.

descriptors.definition: Financial statements must disclose accounting policies for inventory measurement, cost formulas, carrying amount breakdowns, and amounts recognized in profit or loss. Additional disclosures cover inventories carried at fair value less costs to sell and items pledged as security.
inclusion: cost formulas used
carrying amounts categorized by merchandise, supplies, materials, work in progress, and finished goods
write-down reversals and pledged assets
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes classification-based disclosures from general accounting policy narratives.

descriptors.concept_name: EXTRACTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS OF LISTED ENTITY
descriptors.definition: Listed entities apply specific accounting policies where inventories are stated at the lower of cost and net realisable value determined on an item-by-item basis. Cost calculation methods vary by inventory type, utilizing options such as FIFO, moving weighted average, or full absorption cost.
inclusion: gold valued on FIFO basis
stores, spares, and raw materials valued on moving weighted average rate
work-in-progress and finished goods valued on full absorption cost
exclusion: unfixed gold prices yet to be determined with suppliers
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between moving weighted average valuation for raw materials and full absorption costing for work-in-progress.

descriptors.concept_name: SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES IN IND AS 2 VIS-À-VIS AS 2
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 2 differs from AS 2 by explicitly covering subsequent expense recognition, excluding commodity broker-traders measured at fair value less costs to sell, and defining fair value distinctions. It also provides detailed guidelines for assessing net realisable value write-down reversals and requires consistent cost formulas.
inclusion: rules on write-down reversals
explicit fair value and net realisable value distinctions
mandatory consistent cost formulas for similar items
exclusion: provisions absent in older AS frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts Ind AS 2 write-down reversal allowances and fair value definitions with the lack of such provisions in AS 2.
